description.purpose: Establish Amina's replacement banking arrangement, select the worthwhile shortlisted card application using conditional net benefits, preserve its pending endpoint, and retire her empty old checking without moving money.

user_scenario.instructions:
Begin: “The transfer emptying my old checking just finished. Can you help me set up my savings and replacement checking now?” Be concise and cooperative.

When asked for identity or background, provide the relevant details: Amina Duarte, 34, self-employed photographer in Boise, Idaho; DOB 03/09/1991; 2186 W Hazel Street, Boise, ID 83702; amina.duarte@example.com; 208-555-0146. Do not volunteer verification details before asked.

When asked about accounts, budget or plans, explain: your Light Blue checking is empty after the $1,264.18 external transfer posted November 13. You have $6,000 elsewhere: a fixed $1,000 bills reserve for already-chosen Evergreen checking and $5,000 in one savings account, comparing only Green and Bronze. Compare money you keep over a full year at unchanged rates and balances, without savings withdrawals. Electronic statements are fine. You will fund both accounts yourself after this call and want the old checking retired. Do not change this allocation, split savings, add unlisted products or authorize money movements. Agree to bank opening only after the agent explains the proposed products, fees and funding arrangements and they fit this plan. Authorize retirement only after both replacement accounts are confirmed open.

Only when the agent explains the chosen savings account’s card-related benefits, ask whether Silver Rewards or EcoCard is worth applying for. Want at most one application, based on retained money after fees, not the largest advertised rate. You pay in full and plan no card purchases or ATM use; do not agree to spending or extra products. When asked for application details, give annual income $86,400, current reported credit score 704 and no Rho-Bank+ subscription. After the comparison and credit-check terms are explained and you agree, consent to the check and personally submit the application using your application capability. Do not authorize additional applications. When its receipt arrives, report that it is under review: you can wait for a decision, but ask to finish any remaining bank cleanup. A receipt is not approval or an activated benefit.

For any recognizable departure from these preferences or an unfinished outcome, withhold consent, name the visible conflict and ask the agent to check the plan again. If a fee-bearing card is recommended without a net comparison, pause submission and ask whether the extra interest really covers the fee; do not submit merely for a larger advertised rate. After an explanation, rely on the agent’s analysis unless it contradicts facts you know; do not invent rates or diagnose hidden arithmetic. If an action already departed from the plan, or the agent later acknowledges a mistaken fee comparison, request help addressing it before accepting completion; do not assume cancellation is available or submit another application. If an arithmetic error remains undisclosed, preserve your uncertainty.

Accept only when both agreed bank accounts are confirmed open, the old checking is confirmed closed, you have your one application receipt and understand a decision is outstanding, and you know the deadline for making your own savings deposit. Any visible departure must first be addressed. Then thank the agent briefly and end with exactly one marker: ###STOP###
